stories.headline: Toia backs himself among NRL's best centres after premiership triumph
stories.summary: After helping the Sydney Roosters to premiership glory with a standout defensive performance against Bradman Best, Robert Toia tells Isaac Issa he feels he's among the best centres in the NRL.
stories.body:
Robert Toia was reluctant to rank himself among the NRL's top three centres during Grand Final week.

After helping the Sydney Roosters to premiership glory with a standout defensive performance against Bradman Best, he was ready to acknowledge the belief he has in his own ability.

"Everyone has an opinion. But personally, yeah, I like to think I'm the best," Toia told ESPN in the victorious Roosters dressing room.

It was a glimpse of the confidence behind his performance, with Toia still coming to terms with the achievement unfolding around him.

"I'm so speechless," he said.

"I can't believe this is real. It's so surreal."

Toia had been unwilling to nominate his place among the competition's leading centres when asked by ESPN earlier in the week.

On Sunday night, his assignment against Best gave him the opportunity to demonstrate why he belongs in that conversation.

The Newcastle star presented a significant challenge on the game's biggest stage, but Toia embraced the responsibility of containing one of the Knights' most dangerous attacking weapons.

"I just knew how big of an occasion it was, and I just knew the boys wanted me to do a job," Toia said.

"Like you said, Bradman Best is one of the best centres, and I pride myself on being one of the top centres, so I just had to do my job."

His defensive performance provided substance behind that self-belief.

Against an opponent capable of changing a game with a single carry, Toia delivered an important contribution to the Roosters' premiership triumph.

His explanation centred on the responsibility he felt towards his teammates and the respect he held for his opposite number. He understood the challenge, backed himself to meet it and knew what the players alongside him needed.

While Toia was confident in his ability, he remained measured when asked whether the premiership marked the beginning of a long and successful career.

"Hopefully, God willing," he said.

"I'm just taking it day by day, year by year, I guess. I'm hoping my body pulls up sweet."

He was more emphatic about the Roosters' chances of challenging again.

With players departing the premiership-winning squad, next season will bring changes. Toia believes the confidence within the group can carry into its title defence.

"Yeah, I'm so confident," he said.

"There's obviously some boys leaving, but the belief in this group is so massive.

"No doubt that we have the mindset and we have the boys, so we go again."

For now, the next campaign can wait.

Toia has a premiership to celebrate - and a performance on the biggest stage to reinforce his place among the game's leading centres.

stories.headline: NFL Week 4: Big takeaways, questions and fantasy spin from Sunday's games
stories.summary: Our NFL Nation reporters react to all the action, answering the biggest questions coming out of each Sunday game. Here's what we learned from Week 4.
stories.body:
The Sunday slate for Week 4 of the 2026 NFL season kicked off in London between the Colts and Commanders. After a slow start, the Colts recovered to secure a victory abroad.

Back in the United States, the road team won in six of eight matchups during the early window. That included a bounceback win by Patriots QB Drake Maye over the Bills. The Cowboys won a shootout in Houston, and the Rams pulled off an improbable comeback against the Eagles.

In the late window Sunday, the 49ers, Chiefs and Vikings all maintained their perfect records with wins. Minnesota defeated the Dolphins despite having kicker Will Reichard score all of the team's points. And the Seahawks bounced back from last week's loss with a close win over the Chargers.

Our NFL Nation reporters reacted to all the action, answering lingering questions coming out of each game and detailing everything else you need to know for teams that played Sunday. Fantasy football analysts Matt Bowen and Tristan Cockcroft also have fantasy takeaways from each matchup.

Let's get to it with the biggest lessons from Sunday's games.

Jump to:

LAC-SEA | KC-LV

DEN-SF | MIA-MIN

NE-BUF | LAR-PHI | JAX-CIN

DAL-HOU | ARI-NYG | TEN-BAL

GB-TB | NYJ-CHI | IND-WSH

Catch up on Thursday's game:

PIT-CLE

Seattle 30, L.A. Chargers 23
Catch up on the action: Box score | Recap

Seahawks
Can Seattle's backfield continue to withstand Jadarian Price's absence? So far, so good thanks to Emanuel Wilson. A day after the Seahawks put their top pick on IR, Wilson with 120 rushing yards and two touchdowns on 24 touches. He averaged 3.9 yards per carry against a top-10 Chargers run defense. Receiver Rashid Shaheed added a 28-yard rushing touchdown on a toss play, which showed one way Seattle can replace Price's explosiveness. He will miss at least three more games, but Zach Charbonnet is now eligible to come off PUP from his ACL injury. He returned to practice Thursday, and it's unclear if he's ready to play.

Most surprising performance: The defense took a while to slam the door on Los Angeles. That didn't happen until Uchenna Nwosu's strip sack in the final minute. The Seahawks led by as many as 21 points in the second half and had the Chargers on the ropes -- in dropback mode without their No. 1 receiver and starting right tackle. Los Angeles made it a one-score game late in the fourth quarter with three straight scoring drives. -- Brady Henderson

Next game: vs. 49ers (Sunday, 4:25 p.m. ET)

Chargers
Were Justin Herbert's late game heroics an encouraging sign? Herbert started this game terribly, throwing an awful interception on his first play and another one just as bad later in the first half. He ended the first half with just 36 passing yards, the least in his career, according to ESPN Research. Despite playing behind an offensive line of almost all backups in the second half, Herbert looked like the elite player he's typically been. He completed 13-of-16 pass attempts for 144 yards and a touchdown before being strip-sacked on the Chargers' final drive.

Trend to watch: Running back Omarion Hampton's role is decreasing. Hampton was the lead back in Weeks 1 and 2, but his carries have diminished in the past two weeks. He had just nine carries Sunday, second to Keaton Mitchell. Two weeks ago, Hampton had a career-high 23 carries but lost a game-deciding fumble. The difference in carries could be a result of that error. -- Kris Rhim

Next game: vs. Broncos (Sunday, 4:05 p.m. ET)

Fantasy football takeaway: A second-round fantasy pick, Chargers RB Omarion Hampton's stock has slipped to the flex-play tier for upcoming matchups against the Broncos and Chiefs. One week after being outscored by Keaton Mitchell, Hampton played fewer snaps (32% share) and had fewer rushing attempts (9) than Mitchell (38%, 10). -- Cockcroft

Kansas City 30, Las Vegas 27
Catch up on the action: Box score | Recap

Chiefs
Even with a 4-0 start, is now the time for the Chiefs to call Tyreek Hill? The Chiefs exited Allegiant Stadium with their top two receivers having sustained injuries. Tyquan Thornton, who led the Chiefs with 111 receiving yards and two touchdowns, sustained a serious left leg injury in the fourth quarter. In the first quarter, Rashee Rice left the game with a right hamstring injury. In the past month, Hill has indicated his desire to return to the NFL and has posted videos of himself running routes. A reunion between Hill, who sustained a knee injury last season with Miami, and the Chiefs would make sense. Hill's familiarity with the offense could help him get on the field sooner rather than later.

Trend to watch: This stat might seem unbelievable, but it's true: The Chiefs haven't sacked a quarterback in the past three weeks. This is a troubling trend since the Chiefs invested in improving their pass rush in the offseason, including selecting defensive tackle Peter Woods and defensive end R Mason Thomas in the first two rounds of April's draft. -- Nate Taylor

Next game: vs. Chargers (Oct. 18, 4:25 p.m. ET)

Raiders
How concerned should the Raiders be about the run game? The Raiders struggled to gain momentum on the ground yet again. Las Vegas totaled 72 yards on 26 attempts. Outside of his 19-yard carry in the fourth quarter, running back Ashton Jeanty was underwhelming for the third straight week. He had 15 carries for 58 yards. Las Vegas' rushing attack was meant to be the bread-and-butter of this offense. That's why the Raiders made Tyler Linderbaum the highest-paid center in league history and drafted Mike Washington Jr. But right now, it's the team's Achilles' heel.

Key stat to know: Quarterback Kirk Cousins targeted tight ends 22 times against Kansas City. The trio of Brock Bowers, Ian Thomas and Michael Mayer combined for 200 yards and two touchdowns on 15 catches. -- Ryan McFadden

Next game: at Patriots (Sunday, 1 p.m. ET)

Fantasy football takeaway: Raiders TEs Brock Bowers and Michael Mayer each had at least 10 targets and 16 fantasy points, and QB Kirk Cousins has now targeted his tight ends 35% of the time. At that level of usage, Bowers, who has played only two of the Raiders' four games, is in a great situation to challenge Trey McBride for the top TE spot. Bowers is Cousins' go-to guy. -- Cockcroft

San Francisco 24, Denver 14
Catch up on the action: Box score | Recap

49ers
What happens when the 49ers' offense isn't firing on all cylinders? Facing the heat and a stout defense, the 49ers found themselves in a rock fight for the first time this season before a 56-yard touchdown reception by George Kittle sealed the deal. The defense and special teams had some of their best efforts of the season, limiting the Broncos to 4.6 yards per play and coming up with the game's lone turnover. With a trip to Seattle coming, the Niners now know they can win a different kind of game if needed.

Most surprising performance: In a game that felt like it could turn on a takeaway, 49ers special teams ace Siran Neal provided the spark that pushed the Niners to victory. In the third quarter, Neal tracked down Broncos punt returner Marvin Mims Jr. in the open field, held on and forced a fumble that he recovered at Denver's 28-yard line. The Niners scored the game's first touchdown nine plays later to take a lead they would not relinquish. -- Nick Wagoner

Next game: at Seahawks (Sunday, 4:25 p.m. ET)

Broncos
How much will the Broncos be impacted by Pat Surtain II's injury? Surtain, who suffered a leg injury just before halftime, is essentially the starting point for the Broncos' defensive game plan each week -- impacting how they choose coverages, match up on the opponents' best receivers and use certain personnel groupings. Take him out of that equation and their ability to match up becomes significantly reduced. It could force more zone and off coverages for a team that uses Surtain's ability to combat the league's best receivers.

What to make of the QB performance: Bo Nix did have his usual fourth-quarter uptick, throwing his first TD pass deep into the final quarter. But overall, whether it was how he reacted to the 49ers' coverages or the Broncos' approach, there was little work. His accuracy wavered at times, and he finished the day 25-of-42 for 214 yards. -- Jeff Legwold

Next game: vs. Chargers (Sunday, 4:05 p.m. ET)

Fantasy football takeaway: 49ers WR Deebo Samuel Sr. tied a season high with 18 fantasy points, and we saw the versatile deployment that he showcased during his last stint in Kyle Shanahan's offense. Samuel caught five passes for 26 yards and a touchdown, plus he had three carries for 44 yards. He now has at least 15 points in three of four games this season. -- Bowen

Minnesota 15, Miami 10
Catch up on the action: Box score | Recap

Vikings
Are the Vikings really 4-0? Yes they are, despite another tough outing by their offense. As the Vikings failed to score a touchdown for the second time in four games, their defense and special teams continued to lead the way. Kicker Will Reichard remained perfect on the year by going 5-for-5, and the Vikings' defense allowed the Dolphins only eight first downs one week after holding the Buccaneers to 11. The game ended with the crowd giving Reichard a standing ovation, then booing the offense for kneeling on the Dolphins' 1-yard line at the end.

Most surprising performance: With WR Justin Jefferson (ankle) sidelined, Kyler Murray was harried by the Dolphins' pass rush and struggled to find downfield receivers for much of the game. But tight end T.J. Hockenson caught all 13 passes thrown his way, tying his career high, for 119 yards. -- Kevin Seifert

Next game: at Saints (Sunday, 1 p.m. ET)

Dolphins
What did the Dolphins' offense show in their first game without De'Von Achane? The new plan should be finding Ollie Gordon II as much open field space as possible. The second-year back led the team in rushing with a career-high 100 yards and a touchdown on nine carries, including a 53-yard run on third down to set up Miami's first points of the game. Miami's defense played well enough to win, but its offense noticeably held the team back for the second straight game. The Dolphins won't get their first win until their offense finds some sort of repeatable rhythm.

Most surprising performance: The Dolphins were the only team in the league without a sack through the first three weeks of the season, but defensive tackle Zach Sieler ended that drought with a sack on the first play from scrimmage. Miami's defense finished with four sacks in its best performance to date under new coach Jeff Hafley. -- Marcel Louis-Jacques

Next game: vs. Bengals (Sunday, 1 p.m. ET)

Fantasy football takeaway: Vikings TE T.J. Hockenson scored a season-high 24.9 points, catching all 13 of his targets for 119 yards. If WR Justin Jefferson (ankle) is still down next week, Hockenson should be started in a prime matchup versus a Saints defense that has struggled against opposing tight ends. -- Bowen

New England 29, Buffalo 26
Catch up on the action: Box score | Recap

Patriots
Has Drake Maye turned a corner after a shaky start? Absolutely. Maye was effective with his legs and settled into a rhythm early by leading a 97-yard opening TD drive. He was also clutch in leading a game-winning TD drive in crunch time. Two turnovers still hurts -- the first a lost fumble when the pocket collapsed, and the second a fluke play at the end of the second quarter when an inaccurate throw to a diving Romeo Doubs popped up into the air. Maye's eight turnovers still lead the NFL.

Most surprising performance: Mike Vrabel being penalized for unsportsmanlike conduct at the end of the second quarter, which came immediately after CB Marcus Jones was penalized for defensive holding on third-and-16. Vrabel was upset, and the Bills -- getting the ball at the 6-yard line -- capitalized to score a TD three plays later.

Best quote from the locker room: "It gets us back in the race," Vrabel said. "Josh [Allen] is unbelievable, but I felt like Drake went toe to toe with him." -- Mike Reiss

Next game: vs. Raiders (Sunday, 1 p.m. ET)

Bills
How do the Bills fix their issues in man coverage? The Bills' makeshift secondary lost challenge after challenge against the Patriots' receivers in man coverage. Missing Christian Benford, Dee Alford and Jordan Hancock didn't help. But the Patriots' vertical attack exposed weaknesses in outside cornerbacks Maxwell Hairston and Davison Igbinosun. Making his first career start, Igbinosun got beat one-on-one by seldom-used receiver Efton Chism III for the game-winning touchdown.

Most surprising performance: WR Keon Coleman put together arguably his best game as a pro, catching six passes for 115 yards and the Bills' go-ahead TD in the fourth quarter. After DJ Moore exited with a shoulder injury right before halftime, Coleman became Josh Allen's go-to target on third downs. Five of his catches either moved the sticks or resulted in points. -- Nick Suss

Next game: at Rams (Monday, 8:15 p.m. ET)

Fantasy football takeaway: Patriots QB Drake Maye finally showed chemistry with WR Romeo Doubs, targeting him on 9 of 37 attempts. Doubs finished with 23.8 fantasy points. It's the first elite fantasy day by any Patriots WR in 2026, and perhaps the start of a WR3/flex run for Doubs while A.J. Brown heals. -- Cockcroft

L.A. Rams 24, Philadelphia 20
Catch up on the action: Box score | Recap

Rams
Will the Rams figure out how to avoid self-inflicted wounds? As a result of penalties, turnovers and special teams errors, the Rams struggled to get into a rhythm on offense until late in the fourth quarter. The penalties have been an issue this season; through four weeks, the Rams had 10 penalties accepted against them in red zone situations, which is three more than any other team, according to ESPN Research. On Sunday, the penalties came all over the field, as Los Angeles was called for eight penalties for 100 yards. The Rams will continue to struggle closing out wins if they cannot stop their unforced errors.

Most surprising performance: Despite missing Myles Garrett, Aaron Donald and Jaylen Watson, the Rams' defense held the Eagles to 172 total yards and 0-of-12 on third down and 1-of-4 on fourth down. While the Eagles scored 20 points, 17 were scored on drives that started in Rams territory (two interceptions and a short field after a long punt return by the Eagles). -- Sarah Barshop

Next game: vs. Bills (Monday, 8:15 p.m. ET)

Eagles
Are the Eagles in trouble? Injuries are mounting, and with more tough games upcoming, they're facing a critical stretch of the season. The Eagles' defense, coming off a rough game against the Bears, rebounded with a two-takeaway performance in the first half. But a late Rams surge turned a double-digit lead into a disheartening defeat. In the meantime, they lost edge Jonathan Greenard (ankle), cornerback Quinyon Mitchell (knee) and running back Saquon Barkley (hamstring) to go with a host of injuries entering the game. Philadelphia will be limping into next week's game against the Jaguars in London before facing the Panthers and Cowboys.

What to make of the QB performance: Jalen Hurts found little success through the air (12-of-27, 93 yards). He capitalized on strong field position generated by the defense and special teams by tossing a pair of touchdown passes, both to Darius Cooper. But the Eagles were awful on third down, going 0-for-12. Hurts was working uphill without Smith, Barkley, tight end Dallas Goedert and tackle Lane Johnson, who was a late scratch because of personal reasons. But that won't make the result much easier to swallow. -- Tim McManus

Next game: vs. Jaguars (Sunday, 9:30 a.m. ET in London)

Fantasy football takeaway: After missing the past two games with hip and groin injuries, Rams WR Puka Nacua scored a season-high 27.7 fantasy points, catching nine of 12 targets for 125 yards and scoring on a low red zone rushing carry (jet sweep). With Nacua healthy and seeing this type of usage, he's back as an elite WR1 in Sean McVay's system. -- Bowen

Jacksonville 22, Cincinnati 17
Catch up on the action: Box score | Recap

Jaguars
Can the Jaguars keep relying on turnovers on defense? Jacksonville's defense took the ball away twice and should have had a third (a Travis Hunter INT was wiped out by a roughing the passer penalty). That is 10 takeaways in four games, which has helped make up for an inconsistent pass rush. It was part of the Jaguars' identity in 2025, and it's working again a month into 2026. However, injuries are mounting in the secondary (safeties Eric Murray and Caleb Ransaw left the game and cornerback Montaric Brown was inactive). That could impact the defense over the next two weeks.

What to make of the QB performance: It was an efficient day for Trevor Lawrence with 227 yards and one touchdown. The only blemish was missing a wide-open Brenton Strange for what could have been a game-sealing touchdown pass early in the fourth quarter. Instead, the Bengals made a push up until the final minute.

Best quote from the locker room: Jaguars HC Liam Coen on the team's 13 penalties for 125 yards, including 10 for 100 in the first half: "Never been part of anything like that before in my life. I'm not going to say anything to get fined. That was just mental. It was mental. I've just never quite seen something that much the first half of a football game." -- Michael DiRocco

Next game: vs. Eagles (Sunday, 9:30 a.m. ET in London)

Bengals
Can the Bengals withstand losing Ja'Marr Chase for a period of time? Yes, Cincinnati can lean on WR Tee Higgins and TE Mike Gesicki as major receiving options if needed. But if Chase misses any time with a potential concussion (he was ruled out at halftime), that significantly hurts Cincinnati's offense. Not only are the Bengals already down two receivers (Andrei Iosivas, Colbie Young), but Chase also tilts the field like few players in the NFL. Without him for most of the game, Higgins had his second career game with at least 150 receiving yards.

What to make of the QB performance: Joe Burrow did well under a lot of pressure, but he threw two interceptions, including one in the red zone as the Bengals were driving to take the lead early in the fourth quarter. Since the start of the 2024 season, he now has an NFL-high 13 turnovers in the fourth quarter or overtime, per ESPN Research.

Best quote from the locker room: "We had our opportunities the last two weeks, but certainly this isn't Armageddon or anything," Burrow said. "We're still in a great spot." -- Ben Baby

Next game: at Dolphins (Sunday, 1 p.m. ET)

Fantasy football takeaway: Bengals WR Tee Higgins dominated targets (16-of-53) after Ja'Marr Chase's early injury exit, scoring 26.7 fantasy points. With some question about whether Chase can clear the NFL's concussion protocol in time for Week 5, Higgins could elevate to fantasy WR1 status. -- Cockcroft

Dallas 34, Houston 30
Catch up on the action: Box score | Recap

Cowboys
How badly did the Cowboys need this win? Really badly. Since 2000, the Cowboys have not opened a season with just one win in their first four games and made the playoffs. Coming off a debilitating late loss last week, the Cowboys won for just the third time with Dak Prescott as their starting quarterback when trailing by double digits at halftime, per ESPN Research. The Cowboys' offense awoke in the second half, and Prescott delivered a winning drive with a 12-yard TD pass to CeeDee Lamb. Being .500 now doesn't guarantee a postseason spot -- since 2000, they have had 12 2-2 starts and made the postseason in just three of those seasons -- but it gives them some life ahead of next week.

Trend to watch: The Cowboys must figure out a lot of things, but their field goal protection is near the top of the list. For the second straight game, Brandon Aubrey had a long field goal attempt blocked. Last week in Rio, it was a 59-yard attempt from his left side. On Sunday, it was a 62-yard try from his right. The last time the Cowboys had field goal tries blocked in back-to-back games came in 1991. Those Cowboys, however, won both games. These Cowboys split them. -- Todd Archer

Next game: vs. Buccaneers (Thursday, 8:15 p.m. ET)

Texans
Where did it all go wrong? The Texans received the ball with 6:55 left trailing 27-23, and the offense scored a touchdown, giving them hopes of capturing their first win. But the defense completely fell apart on Dallas' subsequent drive, which Dak Prescott capped with a touchdown pass to wideout CeeDee Lamb. Prescott shredded Houston for 335 passing yards while Lamb finished with 17 catches for 189 yards -- puzzling stats considering the defense has three Pro Bowl defensive backs. This season has been the opposite of complementary football. If the offense plays well, the defense doesn't match it. And when the defense plays well, the offense struggles.

What to make of the QB performance: C.J. Stroud continued his high-level play, throwing for 347 yards and two touchdowns. Stroud did his part and led the offense into the end zone late in the fourth quarter. But for the second straight week, the defense failed to close it. -- DJ Bien-Aime

Next game: at Titans (Sunday, 1 p.m. ET)

Fantasy football takeaway: Texans QB C.J. Stroud scored a season-high 23.08 points, and he should be viewed as a matchup-based starter with WR Nico Collins back on the field. Collins, who missed the past two games with a hamstring injury, caught seven of a team-high eight targets for 110 yards and two touchdowns. He is the difference-maker for Houston's pass game. -- Bowen

N.Y. Giants 36, Arizona 24
Catch up on the action: Box score | Recap

Giants
Did Jameis Winston do enough to keep the starting job? This is the up-and-down Winston experience that is expected. Yes, there were two ugly interceptions. But there were also some "Wow!" throws and three touchdown passes. It was his 20th career three-touchdown game. He went 18-of-29 for 250 yards. It wasn't pretty, but it was enough to produce a victory for the second straight week. Winston has been adamant about being judged on wins and losses. This probably bought him some more time with J.J. McCarthy waiting in the wings.

Key stat to know: The Giants scored their first TD in 152 minutes and 56 seconds of game action, a mark of more than 10 quarters. Malachi Fields' 12-yard touchdown reception from Winston late in the second quarter on a broken play ended the drought after 25 drives. New York hadn't scored a touchdown since the fourth quarter of Week 1, when Jaxson Dart was still the quarterback.

Best quote from the locker room: "You know who else came through? Tae Banks. Tae Banks," Giants coach John Harbaugh said of Deonte Banks' game-sealing 98-yard interception return for a touchdown. "He came through with a huge play and after a crazy pass interference." -- Jordan Raanan

Next game: vs. Commanders (Sunday, 1 p.m. ET)

Cardinals
What happened after Arizona's first two touchdowns? The Cardinals had a chance to put Sunday's game to bed early ... like first-quarter early. Up 14-6, Arizona turned the ball over when Marvin Harrison Jr. picked off Jacoby Brissett on the second play of the team's third drive. The offense fell apart from there, gaining 7 total yards until the second-to-last play of the first half. The Cardinals' offensive line, which was creating holes that allowed Arizona's running backs to average 9.0 yards per carry on the first two drives, struggled to spring runs and protect Brissett.

Key stat to know: Eight. That's the number of plays of 10 yards or longer that the Cardinals' defense allowed vs. the Giants. Limiting explosive plays has been a priority for Arizona's defense. The Cardinals gave up six plays of 15 yards or longer in the loss.

Best quote from the locker room: "I just feel like coach was counting on me to make plays and calling my name and I fell up short," said wide receiver Michael Wilson about his seven-catch, 95-yard and zero touchdown performance. "And the only thing I can feel right now is I feel like I lost this football team that game." -- Josh Weinfuss

Next game: vs. Lions (Sunday, 4:25 p.m. ET)

Fantasy football takeaway: Giants WR Malik Nabers finally had that big game working with QB Jameis Winston (23.2 FPTS and 24% target share) ahead of an appealing Week 5 matchup. And TE Isaiah Likely got involved, too (13.6 and 41%). Both warrant places in all fantasy lineups for next week. -- Cockcroft

Baltimore 24, Tennessee 18
Catch up on the action: Box score | Recap

Ravens
What's the concern level regarding Lamar Jackson's injury? Jackson didn't play in the second half after sustaining an ankle injury on the final offensive snap before halftime. It appeared Titans linebacker Jermaine Johnson II landed on the side of Jackson's left ankle. With Jackson remaining in uniform on the sideline, this feels like a case where the Ravens didn't want to risk further injury to him, considering they had a double-digit lead. Still, Baltimore struggled without Jackson. In five drives with backup Tyler Huntley, the Ravens totaled 98 yards, no points and punted four times. That said, if Jackson has to miss any more time, Baltimore has confidence in Huntley, who was 2-0 last season.

Key stat to know: Tyler Loop's 64-yard field goal that ended the first half was the longest in M&T Bank Stadium's 28-year history. It surpassed the previous long by 6 yards. This has been quite a run by Loop, who won last week's game in Rio with a 56-yard field goal as time expired. -- Jamison Hensley

Next game: at Falcons (Sunday, 8:20 p.m. ET)

Titans
Has Carnell Tate emerged as the Titans' top pass catcher? Quarterback Cam Ward threw to Tate more than any other pass catcher, and this year's No. 4 pick delivered. Tate became the first Titans receiver to gain 100 or more receiving yards since Calvin Ridley (131) against the Cardinals on Oct. 5, 2025. Tate also drew an illegal contact call on the team's second drive, which led to their first touchdown. Although he had a few drops and a fumble, he has clearly emerged as the top receiver for Ward, who said last week that he noticed Tate getting open and wanted to increase his targets.

What to make of the QB performance: The stats won't say so, but Ward played much better than he did in the first three games. He seemed more comfortable in the pocket and even stared down the pass rush before delivering the ball to Tate on a third down. Most of Ward's throws were on the money and his only interception wasn't his fault, as the ball bounced off Tony Pollard's hands. He also cleared 200 passing yards for the first time this season. -- Turron Davenport

Next game: vs. Texans (Sunday, 1 p.m. ET)

Fantasy football takeaway: Ravens WR Zay Flowers scored a season-high 25.8 fantasy points this week, but where do we see the wide receiver for Week 5 if QB Lamar Jackson (ankle) is out? If Tyler Huntley gets the start, the Ravens could be more run-heavy. But look for a play-action passing game script, which should create schemed targets for Flowers. He'll stay in the WR2 range. -- Bowen

Green Bay 17, Tampa Bay 14
Catch up on the action: Box score | Recap

Packers
Is this enough to think the Packers are back on track? Well, they needed to go the distance to beat a winless team that started an undrafted rookie quarterback, so it probably won't convince anyone of much. Throw in the loss of one of the Packers' best defensive players, linebacker Edgerrin Cooper to an Achilles injury, and new problems were created. At least this got them to 2-2 with a run of three home games in the next four weeks. Even though the potential loss of Cooper could be difficult, they will get Micah Parsons back at some point.

Most surprising performance: The Packers blew two legitimate scoring chances in the fourth quarter with turnovers. First, running back Kaleb Johnson lost a fumble at the Bucs' 1-yard line with a little more than 9 minutes left. On the next possession, Jordan Love threw an interception at the Bucs' 7-yard line. It marked the first time since a 2013 loss to the Bengals that the Packers had multiple fourth-quarter turnovers with a lead, according to ESPN Research. -- Rob Demovsky

Next game: vs. Bears (Sunday, 1 p.m. ET)

Buccaneers
Can Jalon Daniels keep the Bucs afloat while Baker Mayfield is out? There were some encouraging things about Daniels' performance, even with the two interceptions. Although Zac Robinson didn't do him many favors with playcalling, he orchestrated two touchdown-scoring drives, including one that ended on a 10-yard throw to Kenny Gainwell. On the final drive, Daniels also made clutch passes to Ted Hurst III on fourth-and-1 and Cade Otton on third-and-3. But that drive ultimately ended in an unblocked Evan Williams forcing an interception on fourth-and-11. Daniels finished 19-of-27 for 148 yards with one touchdown and two INTs.

Trend to watch: The Bucs' defense continues to do some bewildering stuff, like surrendering a 31-yard Kaleb Johnson run up the middle with neither Vita Vea nor Josiah Trotter on the field -- the Packers entered Sunday with the league's worst rushing offense. Tampa Bay also had zero sacks against a Packers' offensive line that allowed 34 quarterback hits in Weeks 1-3. Cornerback Zyon McCollum did make a touchdown-saving fumble recovery and cornerback Jacob Parrish intercepted Jordan Love to give them a shot in the end. -- Jenna Laine

Next game: at Cowboys (Thursday, 8:15 p.m. ET)

Fantasy football takeaway: Packers WR Matthew Golden continues to see steady volume, and his red zone usage creates scoring opportunities. Golden, who had 11.7 points this week, has seen at least six targets in each game this season. And he has caught a touchdown in back-to-back games on end zone throws. He should be in the lineup for Week 5. -- Bowen

Chicago 23, N.Y. Jets 12
Catch up on the action: Box score | Recap

Bears
Did Tyson Bagent justify being QB1 for the Bears after Case Keenum's Week 3 strong performance? Keenum, who led the Bears to a rout of the Eagles in Week 3, was officially the starter Sunday, but only because coach Ben Johnson put him at QB for the first snap. After that, Bagent took over and went 25-of-34 for 268 yards. He didn't throw a TD and was picked off once, although three other interceptions were negated by penalties. The Bears leaned on their run game as a result (232 yards) until Bagent got on track in the second half.

Most surprising performance: After maxing out at 10 carries in each of the Bears' first three games, Kyle Monangai carried the load on the ground (30 rushes, 146 yards, 2 TDs) and became the third different Bears player with multiple rushing touchdowns in a game this season. On an afternoon when D'Andre Swift couldn't punch the ball in twice from inside the 3-yard line and later fumbled, Chicago needed everything it got from Monangai to break through on offense. -- Courtney Cronin

Next game: at Packers (Sunday, 1 p.m. ET)

Jets
Were the Jets doomed by injuries or just bad offense? They played without four starters, including RB Breece Hall, but this was inexcusable. QB Geno Smith played his worst game; the third-down offense was terrible (0-for-7); and Garrett Wilson (3 catches, 27 yards) and Kenyon Sadiq (0 catches) were nonfactors. The Jets had 99 total yards before a 58-yard TD strike to Isaiah Williams in the fourth quarter. They're having an identity crisis. The Jets want to be a physical, run-heavy team, but they veer from the plan because of inconsistent execution and/or lack of commitment. They'd better figure it out soon after losing three straight.

Key stat to know: It's over, it's over! Safety Minkah Fitzpatrick picked off Tyson Bagent in the second quarter, ending the longest interception drought in NFL history. The Jets went 20 games and 643 pass attempts without one, dating back to Jan. 5, 2025. It was Fitzpatrick's first full game as a Jet. This is why they traded for him in the offseason -- to make plays on the ball. They could've had four interceptions, but three were nullified by penalties. -- Rich Cimini

Next game: vs. Browns (Sunday, 1 p.m. ET)

Fantasy football takeaway: Backup RBs were the standouts on both teams: Braelon Allen (94% snap and 100% rushing shares and 4.2 YPC) for the Jets and goal-line standout Kyle Monangai (7 goal-to-go carries, 2 TDs, 28.0 total FPTS) for the Bears. Allen is the clear insurance policy for Breece Hall's managers, and Monangai's usage signals flex-play appeal for fantasy moving forward. -- Cockcroft

Indianapolis 30, Washington 13
Catch up on the action: Box score | Recap

Colts
Can the Colts keep winning in ugly fashion? There's a lot to be said for the Colts getting back to .500 after their 0-2 start. But their two victories raise as many questions as reasons for optimism. The performance of QB Daniel Jones in each of the past two games has been concerning, to say the least. After committing three turnovers in a win over the Texans, he was responsible for two more Sunday while the offense was often lethargic. The Colts have shown defensive improvement for the second straight week, but neither of the offenses they've played has showed much explosiveness. Still, getting back on track gives the Colts a chance to recover from their poor start.

Most surprising performance: Defensive tackle DeForest Buckner continues to dominate despite recently coming back from a very delicate neck surgery. Buckner, at 32, was all over the field on Sunday, pressuring Washington's quarterbacks, stuffing the run and more. Buckner chasing down quarterback Marcus Mariota on a scramble was especially impressive, as was his consistent batting of passes at the line of scrimmage. -- Stephen Holder

Next game: at Steelers (Sunday, 1 p.m. ET)

Commanders
Can the Commanders recover from all these injuries? As the saying goes, it's getting late early for the Commanders. They were already playing minus their top four offensive players -- tackle Laremy Tunsil, receiver Terry McLaurin, quarterback Jayden Daniels and guard Sam Cosmi -- and then they lost backup QB Marcus Mariota. The good news for them? They're hopeful Daniels can return in Week 5, but they need McLaurin (hamstring) and Cosmi (concussion) and their returns remain uncertain. And the worst part for Washington: After facing the Giants next Sunday, they play at San Francisco and then host the Eagles and Rams. Injuries plus that schedule equals trouble.

What to make of the QB performance: Athan Kaliakmanis, who was filling in for Mariota, has a big arm and plays with poise, but he's also inexperienced and playing behind a patchwork line. Bad combo. He completed 15 of 33 passes for 186 yards, with a touchdown and an interception. With Mariota injuring the same knee that sidelined him multiple weeks in training camp, the Commanders need to consider signing a veteran to back up Jayden Daniels. However, the line needs to provide more help or it won't matter. -- John Keim

Next game: at Giants (Sunday, 1 p.m. ET)

Fantasy football takeaway: With Mariota (knee) and Daniels (elbow dislocation) both injured, the Commanders' offense is in a precarious spot. Kaliakmanis had his moments -- he was 2-of-6 for 95 yards and a touchdown on deep throws -- but he's a raw prospect. If he has to start in Week 5, downgrade the rest of the Commanders' skill position players across the board. -- Cockcroft

stories.headline: Lakers' Ziaire Williams proposes to longtime girlfriend at Bruno Mars tour
stories.summary: The singer complemented the proposal during his second of five Inglewood shows.
stories.body:
Pop superstar Bruno Mars knows how to put on a good show. But on Friday night, one audience member seemed to steal the show from the 16-time Grammy winner.

As Mars performed "Marry You" during his second night of five in Inglewood, California, for "The Romantic Tour," Los Angeles Lakers forward Ziaire Williams found the perfect moment to make a promise for forever.

On the floor level of SoFi Stadium, Williams got down on bended knee as Mars sang the words "I think I wanna marry you," lining up his question -- "Will you marry me?" -- with the lyrics.

As Williams proposed to his teary-eyed girlfriend, model Paris Timan, Mars blended his singing with his excitement, crooning, "Please say I do I do I do."

After Timan -- who seemed to be in shock -- said yes, Mars continued singing through the song's conclusion while the couple shared a hug as the audience erupted in cheers.

Timan will be part of two new beginnings for Williams. In July, the 25-year-old signed a one-year, $3 million deal with the Lakers after a 2025-26 season in which he posted 10.2 points and 2.4 rebounds per game in 54 games with the Brooklyn Nets.

And the next part? Planning the rest of their lives together. Nothing screams "fairy tale" more than a proposal to a Mars love song.

stories.headline: 2026 WNBA playoffs: Results, takeaways from semifinal Game 1s
stories.summary: How the semifinal series began -- and what Atlanta, New York, Golden State and Las Vegas all need to do in Game 2.
stories.body:
The 2026 WNBA semifinals tipped Sunday with two entertaining Game 1s, with wins for the higher seed in each series.

In the first one, No. 4 Atlanta defeated No. 8 New York 92-82 despite losing All-Star Allisha Gray late in the first half to a hand injury.

Later, No. 2 Golden State hung on to win a semifinal game for the first time in franchise history, beating reigning champion and No. 3 seed Las Vegas 71-60.

Both best-of-five series will continue Wednesday in Atlanta (7:30 p.m. ET, ESPN) and San Francisco (9:30 p.m. ET), respectively.

ESPN's Alexa Philippou and Kendra Andrews break down how both Game 1s were won, as well as keys for the rest of the semifinal series.

MORE: Keys to the semifinals | Strengths, flaws for every team |

Top 25 players | Schedule

(2) Golden State Valkyries 71,

(3) Las Vegas Aces 60

How the game was won: Golden State dominated the boards, outrebounding the Aces 51-23 and outscoring them 20-3 on second-chance points. This is the only the third time in franchise history Las Vegas have been outrebounded by more than 20 in the playoffs. The Valkyries' dominance there kept the reigning champions at an arm's length the entire game. They built as much as an 11-point lead, and fended off every push the Aces made, never letting them get to within five points. Gabby Williams picked up right where she left off in the first-round series against Dallas, finishing with 25 points on 9-of-18 shooting. Golden State held Las Vegas to 33.9% shooting from the field.

What the win means for the Valkyries: They entered this series knowing how important the bench minutes would be: That group stepped up with 27 points to the Aces' five. Kaitlyn Chen was the team's second-leading scorer with 11 points. Aminata Gueye, who signed with the team on Sept. 20, had a breakout performance, finishing with nine points on 4-of-5 shooting and taking on the defensive assignment of guarding A'ja Wilson. Gueye played ony 10 minutes in the first round, but because of Las Vegas' length could play a more critical role in this series. The second unit's performance -- especially Chen -- was particularly crucial for Golden State after Veronica Burton checked out with 7:30 left in the third quarter and did not return.

Who needs to step up for the Aces? The biggest concern currently is the health of Jewell Loyd, who sustained a left leg injury in the first two minutes of the third quarter and by the end of the period was ruled out for the rest of the game. Loyd attempted only two shots and made neither. But with no NaLyssa Smith, whose season ended at the end of August because of a left leg injury, the Aces need Loyd to be healthy in this series. Before the game, Valkyries coach Natalie Nakase had said Loyd was mentioned less in talks about Vegas' big three but should not be discounted for what she means to the team. Loyd scored 11 points in the Aces' series-clinching game in the first round, and they still need her. -- Kendra Andrews

(4) Atlanta Dream 92,

(8) New York Liberty 82

How the game was won: The Dream came out of halftime like a bat out of hell defensively, completely putting the Liberty on their heels. New York had a decent amount of success on the offensive end in the first half, but Atlanta forced turnovers continuously, and converted them into easy buckets. At the half, the Liberty already had 10 turnovers, with the Dream scoring 13 points off them; in the third quarter alone, Atlanta came away with nine steals and scored 16 points off them -- tied for a WNBA playoff record in any quarter. Angel Reese, the recently crowned defensive player of the year, and Jordin Canada led the effort, accounting for three steals apiece, with Canada scoring 12 points in the frame.

New York, which trailed by as many as 16 points early in the fourth, would get back to within five late, but struggled to get the requisite stops down the stretch to pull closer.

What it means for the Dream: This is as good a result as they could ask for, especially given Allisha Gray's injury. A lot has been made of Atlanta's (lack of) depth this season, which could have caused issues with the four-time All-Star being ruled out late in the first half with a left hand injury. But DeWanna Bonner (off the bench) and Canada (playing through foul trouble) showed their veteran experience with a combined 48 points to lead the way. Atlanta took care of business by protecting home court in Game 1, and it will look to do it again on Wednesday for a commanding 2-0 lead when the series shifts to Brooklyn later this week.

Who needs to step up for New York? First and foremost, New York needs to take care of the ball more. Sabrina Ionescu and Leonie Fiebich had five and four turnovers, respectively -- though they were far from the only ones with multiple turnovers. Ionescu also had only one assist -- an area she pointed to for improvement. Jonquel Jones dominated the glass and did a good job facilitating, but the Liberty are at their best when she is aggressive down low, and she finished with just 12 points on 4-9 shooting on the day. New York also had only six total bench points, a fraction of what Bonner scored singlehandedly for Atlanta. -- Alexa Philippou

stories.headline: AFL: Heavyweight trades loom large over AFL free agency period
stories.summary: Essendon and Hawthorn's jostling over Zach Merrett and deals for free agents Zak Butters and Ben King will headline another bumper trade and free agency period.
stories.body:
Essendon and Hawthorn's jostling over Zach Merrett and deals for free agents Zak Butters and Ben King will headline another bumper AFL trade and free agency period.

Brisbane's dual Brownlow medallist Lachie Neale and GWS captain Toby Greene respectively strolled to Collingwood and Geelong after free agency opened on Friday, courtesy of their unrestricted status.

Port Adelaide superstar Butters and Gold Coast key forward King face a longer wait as restricted free agents.

The Power can match any bid for 26-year-old Butters, who nominated the Western Bulldogs as his preferred destination over Geelong, and will want more than the first-round compensation they would otherwise garner.

As league-wide haggling ramps up when the trade period opens on Monday, the Bulldogs may well have to get creative at the negotiating table to satisfy Port.

Gold Coast have similarly canvassed matching a rival bid for King when Hawthorn officially come knocking for the Victorian spearhead.

A bid on Butters or King would generate band one compensation, currently valued at pick five for Port and pick seven for Gold Coast.

Complicating matters, Hawthorn is making another dash at Merrett after Essendon sensationally rejected offers for the gun midfielder in 2025.

The Hawks hold a respectable draft hand, with four draft picks between 15 and 33 on top of future first-round selections in 2027 and 2028.

Merrett, who turned 31 on Saturday, is entering the final year of his Bombers contract and clinched a seventh club best and fairest award after a disastrous two-win season.

With Butters and Merrett spurning Geelong's advances, the Cats have shifted their focus to injury-plagued Essendon defender Jordan Ridley, contracted until 2029, and St Kilda ruckman Rowan Marshall.

St Kilda asked for a player in exchange for Marshall after the contracted 30-year-old requested a trade away to the Cattery for a second straight season.

The Cats were not keen to entertain giving up young half-back Lawson Humphries but talks for Marshall remain ongoing.

In other wheelings and dealings, Gold Coast is expected to trade a late pick for Collingwood veteran Scott Pendlebury if King walks as a restricted free agent so as not to dilute their compensation pick.

Dumped GWS forward and 2024 Coleman medallist Jesse Hogan is also expected to join Collingwood for a late pick rather than waiting for delisted free agency.

Carlton are reportedly trying to prise contracted half-back Lachie Whitfield out of GWS, while trade speculation surrounds Nick Blakey after he and four other Sydney Swans players were banned on the eve of the finals.

Brisbane premiership winger Sam Marshall is eyeing a trade to St Kilda, Luke Pedlar wants a rare switch from Adelaide to Port Adelaide, and Geelong midfielder Jack Bowes is trying to get to Essendon.

Jack Viney, Melbourne's 2021 premiership vice-captain, on Thursday said a deal would be done after he met with West Coast.

Demons coach Steven King told the 32-year-old midfielder he was likely to be on the outer next season despite having two years remaining on his contract.

The free agency period ends on Friday, while the trade window wraps up on October 14.

stories.headline: Who most deserves the Ballon d'Or? Whittling down the 30-man short list
stories.summary: Kylian Mbappé, Lamine Yamal and Harry Kane are the three favorites to win the 2026 Ballon d'Or, but who actually deserves to win it?
stories.body:
For most of the past 15 years, there was really no point in campaigning for the men's Ballon d'Or -- it was going to the more obnoxiously successful of two men, Lionel Messi (eight-time winner) or Cristiano Ronaldo (five). Their personal -- and sometimes club -- rivalry defined the sport, to the point where even a rising star like Kylian Mbappé openly admitted he wasn't as good as them.

"It's not only me who knows that," he told writer Simon Kuper in "The Barcelona Complex." "Everyone knows it. If you tell yourself that you'll do better than them, it's beyond ego or determination -- it's lack of awareness. Those players are incomparable. They have broken all laws of statistics."

"I can't top them" probably isn't the healthiest thing in the world for a megastar to tell himself, but with Messi and Ronaldo finally having aged out of the competition -- Ronaldo hasn't finished in the top three of the voting in the 2020s, and Messi's final win came in 2023 -- now's the time to pounce.

Mbappé wants it. Lamine Yamal has said he wants it. Harry Kane thinks winning it would be "amazing." They're the three betting favorites for the award -- Kane's and Yamal's odds are both at +100 after a recent rise from Yamal, while Mbappé is at a longer +1000 -- but who actually deserves it?

After some late PR campaigns from players and clubs, voting for the award closed on Monday. It will go to the player who achieved the most between the beginning of the 2025-26 club season and the end of the 2026 FIFA World Cup. Thirty players were officially nominated, but based on who has won the award in the past, we can narrow the field pretty quickly.

- Ogden: Does Man City's guilty verdict impact Pep Guardiola's legacy?

- Marcotti: Hard to see how City recover from extraordinary guilty verdict

- Lindop: Liverpool can't afford to be without Isak, Gakpo in October

Eliminate anyone who played for Real Madrid last season

Eliminated: Jude Bellingham, Kylian Mbappé, Vinícius Júnior

I'm sorry, but we have to start here. The three players above are all dynamite, and two have come pretty close to winning the award already -- Mbappé was 192 points behind Messi in 2023, and Vinícius was only 41 points behind Rodri in 2024.

Mbappé is indeed No. 3 in the betting odds, and his scorpionlike quick strike capabilities might make him the most terrifying player in the world. At any point, it feels as if you could be about eight seconds from a Mbappé goal. He's great.

He has also been part of a terribly disappointing club team for two straight years. Since Mbappé joined Real Madrid, the only trophies they've won were the UEFA Super Cup and the FIFA Intercontinental Cup in 2024, trophies tied to accomplishments of the team before his arrival.

Real Madrid have finished behind Barcelona in both of Mbappé's seasons, and after winning the UEFA Champions League in the season before his arrival, they haven't made it past the quarterfinals with him. The Ballon d'Or isn't for club underachievers.

Mbappé is a delicious goal scorer, but his inability to even pretend to contribute in defense has held the team back significantly, especially combined with Vinícius' own refusal to do so. Mbappé did, however, have a fantastic World Cup, which is why he's No. 3 on the list -- he won the Golden Boot with 10 goals and became the competition's all-time leading scorer. But even there, his team lost to Yamal's Spain and Kane's England.

It would feel awfully strange if Mbappé retired without a Ballon d'Or, but he didn't earn it in 2025-26, nor did anyone else on a trophy-less Real Madrid team.

That cuts the list to 27 guys.

Actually, eliminate anyone who didn't win a trophy

Eliminated: Bruno Fernandes, Sadio Mané, Julián Quiñones

Technically, players have taken the Ballon d'Or after a trophy-less campaign, but it's rare. Kevin Keegan did it in 1978, back when it was called the "France Football European Footballer of the Year"; Figo did it in 2000 after leading Portugal to the Euro 2000 semis (and making a seismic move from Barcelona to Real Madrid that summer); and Ronaldo did it after scoring 55 goals in 2013. That's it. That's the list.

We watched Mané win a trophy back in the winter, when Senegal upset Morocco in a contentious Africa Cup of Nations final, but they were stripped of the award in March, so it was technically a trophy-free campaign for him. And though Quiñones scored four goals for Mexico at the World Cup (and 33 for Al Qadsiah in the Saudi Pro League) and Fernandes set a Premier League assists record, the bar for accomplishments in a World Cup year is too high. You need a trophy.

Now we're down to 24.

If you won only one trophy, you had better be an attacker

Eliminated: Marc Cucurella, Gabriel Magalhães, Declan Rice, William Saliba

Sorry, I don't make the rules. (I mean, I am kind of making the rules here, but they're based on history.) The one-trophy guys tend to be goal scorers -- Messi in 2019, the original Ronaldo in 2002, Roberto Baggio in 1993, Jean-Pierre Papin in 1990, Ruud Gullit in 1987, Michel Platini in 1983, Karl-Heinz Rumenigge in 1981, Keegan in 1979.

Arsenal won the Premier League with a fantastic core of midfielders such as Rice and defenders such as Gabriel and Saliba, and Cucurella, a fullback, was nearly error-free during Spain's World Cup run. But none of these guys score much.

That gets them eliminated, and it gets us down to 20 contenders.

When in doubt, eliminate anyone who had a disappointing World Cup (or didn't play in it)

Eliminated: Khvicha Kvaratskhelia, Marquinhos, Nuno Mendes, João Neves, Willian Pacho, Vitinha

In a World Cup year, the Ballon d'Or becomes extremely World Cup-centric. It's why Mbappé still has a prayer this year, and it's a main reason why Messi won in 2023 (after Argentina won 2022's winter World Cup), why Luka Modric won in 2018 (after Croatia's run to the final), why Manuel Neuer finished third in 2014 (after Germany's win), why Andres Iniesta and Xavi Hernandez finished second and third in 2010 (after Spain's win), why Fabio Cannavaro won in 2006 (after Italy's win), and on and on.

Unfortunately for a number of Paris Saint-Germain stars, a lack of World Cup success gets them eliminated. World Cup expansion means Georgia's Kvaratskhelia might have hope of playing there one day, but he didn't this summer, while Marquinhos was part of a disappointing Brazilian squad, Pacho's Ecuador bowed out in the round of 32, and Mendes, Neves and Vitinha were all part of a Portugal team that was supposed to contend and didn't. (I guess you could say that Ronaldo got four of his Portuguese teammates eliminated from this competition, too.)

This knocks our list all the way down to 14 remaining players.

You have to be the best player on your club team (or have a case that you are)

Eliminated: Luis Díaz, Pau Cubarsí, Fabián Ruiz, Ferran Torres, Dayot Upamecano

It seems fair, right? Cubarsí is a ridiculously sound center back, especially for a 19-year-old, and Upamecano is a major key to Bayern Munich's high-wire attacking style. Díaz proved his incredible "glue guy" characteristics when he left Liverpool for Bayern and the former fell apart, while the latter achieved a new level of attacking prowess. But few would make the case that these guys are better than Barça's Yamal or Raphinha, or Bayern's Kane or Michael Olise.

Torres, meanwhile, scored the World Cup-winning goal, but Barça let him leave for PSG. So, let's cross these five off our list. Now we're down to nine.

You should be among the top 3 in your position

Eliminated: Ousmane Dembélé, Lautaro Martínez, Lionel Messi

The final nine are all extremely accomplished and talented, so we have to raise the bar even higher. Using the summer's FC 100 voting, we can eliminate Martínez (No. 6 center forward), Messi (No. 5 wide forward) and Dembélé (No. 4 center forward). All three had excellent seasons and/or World Cup campaigns, but others have just been a little bit better in 2025-26. That gets us down to six.

Has anyone in your position ever won the Ballon d'Or?

Eliminated: Achraf Hakimi

Sometimes a non-attacker can transcend the counting stats and win the award. Rodri did, after all, in 2024 following the success of both Spain and Manchester City, and Modric won in 2018 after combining major club success (Real Madrid) with a World Cup run (Croatia). Cannavaro was among the best defenders of the 2000s and rode a World Cup title to victory over Italian teammate Gianluigi Buffon (also not a forward, obviously) in 2006. But no fullback has yet taken the award.

That's apparently a bridge too far. The closest thing was when a sweeper such as Matthias Sammer (1996) or Franz Beckenbauer (1972 and 1976) did the deed, but sweepers still aren't fullbacks, and that was three and five decades ago. Hakimi is the best fullback in the world and has been for a while, but he's not getting the nod.

We're down to five.

How was your club season?

Eliminated: Rodri

Watching Rodri in person at the World Cup was an incredible experience. He saw every potential counterattack against Spain developing 10 seconds in advance and was always in place to intercept the ball before it could start moving in the other direction. He was a timepiece, always keeping Spain from moving too slowly or too quickly. He probably benefited a bit from the slower pace of international play, but he was note-perfect during the tournament and deserved the Golden Ball award.

However, that all came on the heels of a club season in which he started only 17 league games for Manchester City while still trying to return to full form after his 2024 knee injury. The only reason he's on the list is because of the World Cup, and the four remaining guys on this list combined club success with great World Cup performances.

Your finalists

This process of elimination has left us with four potential winners, listed alphabetically:

Erling Haaland, 26, Manchester City/Norway

Relevant stats (club and country): 64 matches (2.19 PPG), 5,146 minutes, 58 goals, 11 assists from 45 chances created, World Cup quarterfinal, two trophies (FA Cup, Carabao Cup)

Harry Kane, 33, Bayern Munich/England

Relevant stats: 65 matches (2.60 PPG), 5,220 minutes, 73 goals, eight assists from 80 chances created, World Cup third place, three trophies (Bundesliga, German Cup, German Supercup)

Michael Olise, 24, Bayern Munich/France

Relevant stats: 69 matches (2.54 PPG), 5,314 minutes, 27 goals, 34 assists from 170 chances created, World Cup fourth place, three trophies (Bundesliga, German Cup, German Supercup)

Lamine Yamal, 19, Barcelona/Spain

Relevant stats: 57 matches (2.46 PPG), 4,574 minutes, 25 goals, 20 assists from 131 chances created, World Cup champion, three trophies (World Cup, LaLiga, Spanish Supercopa)

Actually, listing each player's relevant stats gives me an opportunity to address one of this year's primary Ballon d'Or controversies: the non-inclusion of Raphinha, Yamal's Barça teammate -- and maybe the hottest player in the world right now -- on the 30-man short list. Thirty players is a lot, and Raphinha had an obvious case, but in the time frame around which the award is based, he played only 40 matches and scored 21 goals with eight assists. He battled injuries and form, he barely played for Brazil at the World Cup (130 minutes, zero goals and assists), and he didn't really catch fire until the time frame ended. Consider him an early front-runner for 2027 (though I've already made my prediction in that race).

The betting odds tell us that two of these four players are far more likely to win than the other two, but all four have solid cases.

The case for Haaland

Haaland enjoyed another strong club season, scoring 38 goals with nine assists in all competitions. That almost sounds underwhelming by his standards, but it is still fantastic for someone in the best league in the club universe. Haaland might have enjoyed himself more than anyone else at the World Cup. His seven goals were the most by a World Cup debutant since 1974 (Poland's Grzegorz Lato), and he led Norway to its best-ever finish, a quarterfinal run that included a win over Brazil. (Naturally, he scored both of Norway's goals in that match.)

Haaland was also a bit of a pop culture phenomenon, buying cowboy hats, eating pastrami sandwiches and basically winning over every casual American sports fan. The World Cup belonged to him as much as anyone, and that usually earns you lots of Ballon d'Or votes. His case is likely dinged by both Manchester City's second-place finish to Arsenal in the Premier League and the dark clouds of the City scandal (which had nothing to do with him). But I was very surprised to see his odds for the award at only +4000, tied for eighth with Cubarsí, Dembélé, Olise and Bellingham. He'd be in my top five at worst.

The case for Olise

For my money, Olise is the best player in the world at the moment. That doesn't automatically mean he should win, and it's partially because of how he has started this new season. He already has eight goals and three assists in seven matches for Bayern, and when France needed a spark against Belgium this week in the UEFA Nations League, guess who sprang off the bench and immediately made the difference? But I was already starting to believe in his superiority last season.

Olise scored 22 goals with 26 assists in all competitions -- six to Kane -- for Bayern in 2025-26, a season in which he established himself as the best creator in the world. His touch and vision are sublime, and when it's time for him to do it himself, he's more than OK with doing that.

As with Haaland, Olise's odds are +4000, which is to say he's obviously not going to win it. But he'd be in my top three. He led the World Cup in assists with seven (no one else had more than four), and really, only a finishing slump held him back: He attempted 20 shots worth 2.5 xG, but none went in the net. But that's fine. For those of us in the Olise Is the Best in the World club, he can remain our little secret for a little while longer.

The case for Yamal

This is an award for 2025-26, but the case for Yamal almost has to start with Spain's current 40-match (and more than four-year) unbeaten streak. It correlates almost perfectly with the emergence of Yamal. He played 18 minutes in Spain's last defeat -- a 1-0 friendly loss to Colombia in March 2024 and his fifth appearance for Spain as a 16-year-old -- but during this unbeaten streak, he has started 28 of 40 matches. In this span, he's fourth on the team in minutes (2,305), third in goals (eight), second in shots on goal (36), progressive carries (320) and completed crosses (24) and first in assists (12), chances created (55), line-breaking passes received (297), ground duels won (184) and fouls suffered (44). Hell, he is also second in successful tackles (52) and third in ball recoveries (117).

Yamal wasn't even at full strength during the World Cup, having rushed back from injury, but he still played 615 of 750 minutes, and his mere presence out wide stretched and stressed defenses in ways that opened up opportunities for others. He was content playing more of a supporting role, refused to force the issue and lifted his second major international trophy before his 20th birthday.

Yamal has been the most valuable player on both the most successful international team of the 2020s and the team that has won the last two LaLiga crowns. And his magnetic personality, which comes through in virtually any interview, certainly doesn't hurt his Ballon d'Or cause. Putting together a career that rivals Messi's or Ronaldo's will take a level of longevity that we don't yet know he has, but at worst he's the second-most successful teenager ever behind Pele (who not only won a World Cup but also had two 50-goal campaigns).

The case for Kane

I'm finishing this list with Kane because, honestly, his is the easiest case to make. Yamal seems to be picking up momentum in the race, at least if betting odds are to be believed (and they frequently are), and if he wins it will be hard to say it was unjust. But look again at the stats above. Kane played eight more matches and over 600 more minutes than Yamal -- which is to say, he stayed healthier than a player 14 years his junior -- and he produced 81 combined goals and assists, a full 36 more than Yamal.

Does he play for one of the two most talented and prolific attacks in the world? Obviously. But so does Yamal!

Kane is England's all-time leading goal scorer and has the second-most goals in the history of the Premier League, but he achieved a new level of prowess in his 16th professional season. He scored over 60 club goals in all competitions for the first time, then he scored six goals in seven matches while leading England to the World Cup semifinals for the second time.

You could easily say that, when you're in doubt regarding whom to vote for, you should choose the older player who might not get another chance. But you don't even need to use that as a tiebreaker for Kane against Yamal because I don't think it's tied. He won nearly as much as Yamal at the World Cup, won every domestic trophy with Bayern and posted far superior statistics.

If I had a guess, I'd say Yamal wins at this point because of the late PR push. If I had a vote, however, I'd go with Kane.

stories.headline: USMNT's young stars shine to give Pochettino 'fantastic problem'
stories.summary: USMNT coach Mauricio Pochettino said that the number of players performing at a high level is "a fantastic problem to have" after teenagers Cavan Sullivan and Julian Hall propelled the USMNT to 3-0 win over rivals Mexico on Saturday.
stories.body:
GLENDALE, Ariz. -- United States men's national team coach Mauricio Pochettino said that the number of players performing at a high level is "a fantastic problem to have" after teenagers Cavan Sullivan and Julian Hall propelled the USMNT to 3-0 win over rivals Mexico on Saturday.

The U.S. endured a difficult first half, and scored completely against the run of play in the 28th minute when Hall converted from close range after Mexico keeper Raúl Rangel spilled Gio Reyna's low cross right in front of goal.

- Cavan Sullivan has arrived: U.S. phenom's goal caps a memorable win over Mexico

- Márquez bemoans 'terrible mistakes' as Mexico humbled by USMNT

- USMNT player ratings: Sullivan, Hall 9/10 in big win vs. Mexico

The USMNT began to make more headway in the second half, and doubled its lead in the 62nd minute when Sullivan intercepted a pass from Rangel, and chipped the ball into the net from 35 yards out. The match lost its edge when Mexico's Mateo Chávez was red carded in the 67th minute following a scrap with Sebastian Berhalter.

Malik Tillman finished off the scoring in the 84th minute, latching onto another wayward Mexico pass to firing into the net.

Hall, 18, is just the third USMNT player to score in his first three national team appearances, while 17-year-old Sullivan became the youngest scorer in USMNT history.

"I think it's a fantastic problem for us," Pochettino said about the performances of his team's young players. "I think we will take the right decision in the right moment, but I think it's a very good problem to see.

"Now it's not a moment at all, but yes, we appreciate that situation and of course hope that we will be in that situation that young players perform in the way that they deserve to be with us."

Pochettino also pronounced himself pleased with the way his side weathered Mexico's early pressure.

"I think that this, overall, was a great opportunity to discover ourself, to see ourselves in a difficult game with a very good team. Again, Mexico is a great team," Pochettino said.

"Yes, I think two different maybe halves. The first half I think Mexico started really well. They forced us to play back. We never connected. We were losing all the duels. And then we start to grow after 15, 20 minutes. And I think it was a good lesson the first half because it was the sense of work all together, suffer together even when you are not playing well in the way that you plan to play."

But Pochettino couldn't help but admire the performance of Sullivan, who impressed with his work on both sides the ball.

"I think he's a talented player with enormous quality, but with a very good balance, in possession and out of possession," Pochettino said about Sullivan. "He's a fighter, he's a warrior. It's difficult to find this type of player with a tremendous quality.

"And then I think Cavan showed in possession with the ball on the field [and] when he need to be chasing people and recover the ball. That is my impression after maybe three weeks together. And that is unbelievable, to have a player like this. I think it's a fantastic news for USA. Hope that continues in that way."

Pochettino was careful to laud Sullivan's young teammates as well, who have largely impressed during this window.

"It's a big moment because we need to be right with them," Pochettino said about the win, and the path forward. "We need to protect them. We need to support them. Our responsibility now is that this group of talented players grow in the right direction."

stories.headline: UEFA receives Real Madrid dossier on Barcelona-Negreira case
stories.summary: UEFA has received "a substantial amount of documents" from Real Madrid related to its ongoing inquiry into the Negreira case, European football's governing body said on Thursday.
stories.body:
MADRID -- UEFA has received "a substantial amount of documents" from Real Madrid related to its ongoing inquiry into the Negreira case, European football's governing body said on Thursday.

Payments made by Barcelona to companies linked to José María Enriquez Negreira -- the former vice-president of Spain's Technical Committee of Referees -- over two decades have been subject to a UEFA investigation since 2023, while there is also an ongoing Spanish criminal case.

Barcelona have said the payments, which totaled over €7 million ($7.9m), were made for technical refereeing reports.

- Ronaldo's Portugal walkout is nothing new; he has a long history of rows with coaches

- Source: Mbappé to be available for Clásico

- Raphinha back at Barça, injured in Brazil game

"UEFA can confirm that it has received from Real Madrid CF a substantial amount of documents related to the ongoing investigation into FC Barcelona in the matter involving José María Enríquez Negreira," UEFA confirmed in a statement on Thursday.

"The UEFA Ethics and Disciplinary Inspectors have also received these latest documents which they will assess as part of their ongoing review."

Real Madrid said the dossier included "extensive documentation and evidence regarding events of extraordinary seriousness, which directly affect the integrity of the competition and confidence in the refereeing system."

"Real Madrid C.F. considers it essential that, now that UEFA has this documentation, the investigation proceeds with the utmost urgency until its full conclusion, and that the competent bodies take the appropriate decisions in accordance with the severity of the verified facts," the club said.

"Our club will continue to actively collaborate with UEFA and take all actions within its power to clarify events that it deems incompatible with the principles of integrity, transparency, and fair play that should govern European football."

In May, Madrid president Florentino Pérez said that the club was gathering evidence to submit a dossier to UEFA.

Having previously adopted a conciliatory tone with Barcelona -- saying in 2024 that the two clubs "have to help each other" as they worked together on the proposed European Super League -- Pérez has since been extremely critical of his LaLiga rivals.

"They've stolen seven league [titles] from me," Pérez said in May.

In a statement, Barcelona emphasized that Thursday's development did not equate to "any new proceedings."

"The proceedings were initiated in 2023, with the appointment of two investigators who have since carried out the action they deemed appropriate," Barcelona said. "The Club has always complied with all their requests. These proceedings have not been reopened because they have never been closed.

"The UEFA statement confirms receipt of documentation submitted by Real Madrid and indicates that the investigators will assess it within the framework of the existing investigation. The same text expressly refers, on two occasions, to an investigation and a review that are 'ongoing.' It therefore does not announce the opening, reopening, or reactivation of any proceedings, nor does it contain any assessment of the substance or value of the documentation provided.

"It is up to the investigators to determine what action, if any, they consider appropriate regarding this documentation. As of today, they have not made any new requests to FC Barcelona nor have they forwarded Real Madrid's complaint to the Club. Should they do so, the Club will respond accordingly, as it has done up to now.

"In accordance with the applicable legislation governing this matter, these proceedings are subject to the outcome of the criminal case currently being heard in Spain and will continue to be so."

stories.headline: A fairytale Knights run ends in a Newcastle nightmare
stories.summary: The Sydney Roosters' 19-18 victory delivered the premiership farewell Daly Cherry-Evans had chased, while leaving the Knights one point short of completing their fairytale run.
stories.body:
For a moment, Kalyn Ponga made Newcastle believe the fairytale had one more chapter.

A loose Roosters tap-back, a burst into open space and a sprint almost the length of the field. Suddenly, the Knights led 12-0 and a city that had waited 25 years for another grand final could begin to imagine the ultimate reward.

Instead, Newcastle were left to contemplate how close they had come.

The Sydney Roosters' 19-18 victory delivered the premiership farewell Daly Cherry-Evans had chased, while leaving the Knights one point short of completing their remarkable transformation.

Yet the explanation for Newcastle's heartbreak lay well before the final frantic minutes. Their early lead had concealed a problem that became increasingly difficult to escape: they were spending too much of the decider defending.

The Knights had the moments. The Roosters kept making them work.

Francis Manuleleua's opening try showed the value of Newcastle's willingness to attack, with Fletcher Sharpe finding his backrower on a strong line. Ponga then supplied the kind of individual intervention capable of defining a Grand Final.

His long range try was particularly extraordinary because of the work that preceded it. The Knights captain was repeatedly involved, covering threats behind his defensive line while remaining central to Newcastle's attack.

But even Ponga could not keep turning survival into points.

At halftime, Newcastle led 12-6 despite making 35 more tackles. Sydney had enjoyed 57% of possession and completed 21 of 23 sets. That disparity mattered more than the Knights' advantage suggested.

Every defensive stand bought Newcastle another chance. Too few of those chances bought their defenders a rest.

The Roosters' territorial pressure meant the Knights repeatedly had to begin again from deep inside their own half. Defusing a kick or stopping a raid was only the first part of the task; finding enough ground to change the next possession was just as important.

Sydney's work through the middle made that difficult. As the match wore on, Newcastle's attempts to shift the ball carried an increasing risk: an error would surrender possession before they had escaped trouble.

This was the tension at the heart of the contest. The Knights needed the ball to relieve the pressure, but the pressure was making it harder to use the ball effectively.

Billy Smith's second half try drew Sydney level. Mark Nawaqanitawase, whose improvised finish had brought the Roosters back into the match before halftime, later completed his double.

Newcastle's resistance had kept the contest alive. Sydney's persistence had changed who controlled it.

Then came Cherry-Evans' field goal.

The veteran's strike pushed the margin beyond a converted try, a decision whose value became clear when Greg Marzhew's late score brought Newcastle back within one point.

For all the attacking talent around him, this was the contribution the Roosters had recruited Cherry-Evans to provide - recognising what the game required and delivering it.

At 37, in his final NRL appearance before joining Hull FC, he finished with a second premiership, 15 years after his first with Manly.

Ahead of the decider, Cherry-Evans had explained how experience had changed his approach.

"I'm obviously more mature, so I have a better understanding of what the team needs," he told the media.

His farewell also gave the result an extra layer of significance. Sandon Smith had left the Roosters following Cherry-Evans' arrival, finding an opportunity in Newcastle that developed into a central role in their premiership push.

The Knights' season had demonstrated how much a fresh opportunity could unlock. Smith, Sharpe and Ponga gave Newcastle a combination capable of troubling opponents in different ways, even after Dylan Brown's ACL injury forced another adjustment.

That progress will matter once the immediate disappointment fades.

Justin Holbrook's side reached the decider through sudden-death victories over South Sydney, the Warriors and Penrith. Their run demanded belief as well as execution, and neither disappeared when the Grand Final began to turn against them.

Their late response ensured Sydney had to finish the job.

But Newcastle could not quite turn that refusal to surrender into one final escape.

For the Roosters, experience helped deliver the ending they wanted. For the Knights, the cruelty was in getting close enough to see theirs.

A season that restored Newcastle's belief ended with a premiership one point beyond reach.
